_comment: COST-CONSCIOUS SETTINGS - Aggressive cost savings profile.
Defaults to Haiku for most tasks. Restricts expensive operations.
"haiku" is Haiku 5.5 on the Anthropic API (Claude Code v2.1.293+): $0.10/$0.50 up to 100K prompt tokens, $0.50/$2.50 above, priced per request -- keep sessions short so prompts stay under 100K.
On Claude Platform on AWS, Bedrock, Google Cloud (Google managed, formerly Vertex AI) and Foundry "haiku" is legacy Haiku 4.5 ($1/$5, 200K) -- set ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL to pin it.
Best for: solo devs on tight budgets, routine maintenance, simple tasks.
Trade-off: lower quality on complex reasoning, more turns for hard problems.
Read(...) deny rules keep Claude's file tools out of deps, build output and secrets (.claudeignore is not a Claude Code feature).

modelSettings sets Haiku 5.5's auto-compact window to 100,000 tokens, the lowest allowed, so compaction fires near its 100K price line (v2.1.288+). It is not a cap: whether compaction fires just under or at 100K is not documented, one request after a large tool result can still cross the line and bill 5x on the whole request, and each compaction is itself a request. The entry matches only Haiku 5.5, so where "haiku" resolves to Haiku 4.5 it does nothing (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#modelsettings, read 2026-11-03).

env: CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_TURNS caps the number of agentic turns when no limit is passed; the docs call it equivalent to --max-turns, which the CLI reference lists as print mode only (claude -p), and do not describe it as limiting interactive sessions (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars and https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference, read 2026-11-01).
